pageCache.pageTitle: Curzon & Fawood Nursery Schools & Family Wellbeing Centre - Home
pageCache.text:
Family Wellbeing Centre
Welcome to Curzon and Fawood Nursery Schools
& Family Wellbeing Centre
Curzon Nursery has been serving local families and the community since the 1930s. While our Fawood site is much newer by comparison, our commitment to high-quality education remains at the heart of our daily routine, even as times have changed.
A video footage capturing a day in the life of children at Curzon Crescent Nursery, filmed in 1955.
//www.youtube.com/embed/y3bwuS6vgs0#t=0.5
We're working to update our website. More exciting content coming soon...
Our Vision: Everyone is a learner
Sustainability
Sustainability
Build lasting behaviours and relationships within our community to tackle the Climate Crisis.
Promote education and volunteering that will enable families to lead economically sustainable lives.
Equity
Commit to an anti-racist, inclusive approach to education that recognises individual needs and experiences.
Build a safe and healthy community where personal goals and family aspirations are achieved.
Technology
Technology
Support and educate children, young people and their family to embrace life in a technologised society.
To actively engage in tech for good and creativity.
Creativity
Learn how to find creative solutions to thrive in the rapidly changing world.
Engage in a learning community that builds confidence, makes connections, imagines and communicate ideas.

pageCache.pageTitle: Curzon & Fawood Nursery Schools & Family Wellbeing Centre - Welcome
pageCache.text:
Welcome
We are one team across two locations—Curzon Nursery and Fawood Nursery—just a 15-minute walk apart. Together, we form a unique partnership with the only Family Wellbeing Centre in Brent that operates in collaboration and within the same building as the nursery schools. This integrated approach allows us to provide a seamless, holistic service to support local families and strengthen our community.
Curzon Nursery
At Curzon, our expansive garden offers endless opportunities for outdoor exploration, where children engage with the natural world. The garden features a pond, a music room, a treehouse, a mud kitchen, and even a group of friendly hens in the chicken coop, who greet the children each day as they arrive and leave.
Curzon Nursery
Fawood Nursery
The award-winning design of our building at Fawood offers a distinctive space that lets in fresh air, creating a comfortable environment while protecting the children from harsh weather as they move in and out of the classroom.
Fawood Nursery

pageCache.pageTitle: Curzon & Fawood Nursery Schools & Family Wellbeing Centre - SEND
pageCache.text:
SEND
Every child has unique qualities and needs that are important to us. We are dedicated to providing the necessary support to help each child develop to their full potential, ensuring they feel comfortable and valued in the classroom as they explore, play, and learn.
Here is an example of a One Page Profile for each child in our Rainbow Class.
Local Authorities and schools are required to publish and keep under review information about services they expect to be available for the children and young people with Special Educational Needs and/or disabilities (SEND) aged 0-25. This is known as the ‘Local Offer’.
The intention of the Local Offer is to improve choice and transparency for families. It will also be an important resource for parents in understanding the range of services and provision in the local area. Information is published as part of the SEND reforms under the Children and Families Act 2014.
Brent Council's Local Offer can be found here:
www.brent.gov.uk/localoffer

pageCache.pageTitle: Curzon & Fawood Nursery Schools & Family Wellbeing Centre - Early Years Pupil Premium
pageCache.text:
Early Years Pupil Premium
What is the Early Years Pupil Premium (EYPP) From 2015 all early years settings and child-minders are able to claim extra funding through the EYPP to support children’s development, learning and care.
We use the extra funding to enhance the quality of early year’s education that we provide for your child and the learning opportunities on offer during the school year. This could include special resources, visits, interventions or additional specialist help.
It is recognised that high quality early education influences how well a child goes on to achieve in primary and secondary school.
All families will be asked to fill in an eligibility form when their child joins the nursery; this enables us to claim the funding. Eligibility is checked simply using a parent/carers National Insurance number.

pageCache.pageTitle: Curzon & Fawood Nursery Schools & Family Wellbeing Centre - Early Years Foundation Stage Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Local government funded nursery schools
Curzon and Fawood are nursery schools. Our commitment goes beyond everyday childcare. Alongside fun and play in a safe, nurturing environment, we offer a structured, curriculum-based program led by qualified teachers. This approach supports children's development and prepares them confidently for their transition to primary school.
Why is a maintained nursery school special?
Curzon and Fawood Nursery are local government maintained schools. We are different to private and independent nursery is that our top and most important business is Early Years Education for the children, not profit. Our day-to-day decisions are based on the education of the children, from how well they adapt from their first day with us and prepare them for primary school.
Less than 400 maintained nursery schools still remain across the UK, and these numbers have been gradually eroded over the years. Unlike nursery classes attached to primary schools we have teachers and headteacher who are early years trained. As early years specialist, our focus is on delivering learn-and-play-age-appropriate education to children at a crucial stage of development, which requires a different set of approaches.
We are inspected under the same Ofsted criteria as primary schools, rather than those used for early years settings in the private and voluntary sector.
Openness and regulated by law
As government funded maintained nursery schools we operate under the guidelines set by the Department of Education and Ofsted. Some of the key guiding principles abiding us are:
Curriculum
We offer a range of areas for learning from guided group sessions to Free-Flow.
*Free Flow is when the curriculum is taught across the indoor and outdoor learning environments both child led and adult led. Provocations is what we call the adult led intended learning.
Communication & Language
Listening, attention, speaking
Personal, social & emotional development
Attachment, conflicts in play, kindness
Physical development
Fine and Gross motor skills
Comprehension, phonics, writing (making marks and scribbles)
Spatial reasoning, number, measurement
Understanding the World
Natural processes, living things and materials, earth and space, people, culture and community
Expressive Arts & Design
Creating with natural materials, being imaginative and expressive

See our Core Planning here.
